From aca19723604c232ffc6376c1c6cd9c8a12158dcc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Gao Xiang <gaoxiang25@huawei.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2018 11:39:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "staging: erofs: disable compiling temporarile"

This reverts commit 156c3df8d4db4e693c062978186f44079413d74d.

Since XArray and the new mount apis aren't merged in 4.19-rc1
merge window, the BROKEN mark can be reverted directly without
any problems.

Fixes: 156c3df8d4db ("staging: erofs: disable compiling temporarile")
Cc: Matthew Wilcox <willy@infradead.org>
Cc: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Chao Yu <yuchao0@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Gao Xiang <gaoxiang25@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/erofs/Kconfig b/drivers/staging/erofs/Kconfig
index 7f209b32228f..c8521d71039b 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/erofs/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/staging/erofs/Kconfig
@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 
 config EROFS_FS
 	tristate "EROFS filesystem support"
-	depends on BROKEN
+	depends on BLOCK
 	help
 	  EROFS(Enhanced Read-Only File System) is a lightweight
 	  read-only file system with modern designs (eg. page-sized
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/staging/erofs/Kconfig`**
   - The dependency for the `EROFS_FS` configuration has been changed from `depends on BROKEN` to `depends on BLOCK`. This modification indicates that the EROFS filesystem support is now dependent on the BLOCK subsystem rather than being marked as broken.

### Relationships

- The patch is a revert of a previous commit that disabled the compilation of the EROFS filesystem by marking it as BROKEN. By changing the dependency back to BLOCK, the patch effectively restores the ability to compile the EROFS filesystem, indicating that the issues that led to the BROKEN mark are no longer applicable. This change suggests that the necessary components (XArray and new mount APIs) are now in a stable state, allowing for the EROFS filesystem to be compiled and used without issues.

Cc: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>

Signed-off-by: Gao Xiang <gaoxiang25@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The EROFS filesystem was initially marked as BROKEN due to the lack of integration of the XArray and new mount APIs in the 4.19-rc1 merge window, which prevented it from being compiled successfully. This indicated that the filesystem was not in a stable state for use at that time.

Reason:
